papers.abstract: The sum of large Pomeron loops in QCD, based on the $t$-channel unitarity and on the solution of the Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) equation in the saturation region, has been combined with the AGK (Abramovsky, Gribov and Kancheli) cutting rules to obtain multiplicity distributions with KNO (Koba, Nielsen and Olesen) scaling and an entropy equal to the logarithm of the gluon structure function. We reexamine these distributions for the BK amplitude and for dipole-dipole scattering. The KNO functions that follow from the Gaussian representation of the asymptotic series have log-normal and not Gaussian tails, $\lnΨ_{\rm BK}\simeq-\frac{1}{2}\ln^2ξ$ and $\lnΨ_{\rm dd}\simeq-\frac{1}{4}\ln^2ξ$, and we give them in closed form in terms of the Lambert function. They are log-normal mixtures of the distributions of one and two BFKL cascades, and the summation is not unique. The KNO scaling requires that power-like factors in the coefficients of the series be discarded, and the alternative contour representation leads to functions that change sign. We then test the approach in two exactly solvable models in zero transverse dimensions. In the unitary toy model we confirm that the resummed series reproduces the exact $S$-matrix to within 2.5-10%, while the $S$-matrix changes by many orders of magnitude. Nevertheless, the multiplicity distribution obtained from the same series with the AGK rules agrees with the exact one only as long as both cascades are dilute. At higher energies the exact mean grows as a power of rapidity, the KNO scaling is absent, and the entropy in the rest frame of the target grows as one half of the logarithm of the mean multiplicity. The amplitude is determined by rare configurations of the cascades and the multiplicity by the typical ones, so that the agreement of the amplitudes does not validate the multiplicity distributions.

papers.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
papers.authors: Niven Achenjang; Katharine Woo
papers.abstract: Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture.   We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

papers.title: Operator uncertainty and cross-domain information in quantum signals: Second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design
papers.authors: Mostafizur Rahaman Laskar; Sajad Daei; Gabor Fodor; Mikael Skoglund; Franco Nori
papers.abstract: We derive second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design by combining entropic uncertainty relations with the covariance description of continuous-variable systems. For any state with finite second moments and entropies, the mutual information between the arrival time and the transverse wave number, which are compatible observables from different canonical pairs, is bounded above by the logarithm of twice the smaller of the time-frequency and position-wave-number uncertainty products. We demonstrate that a Gaussian wave packet with a bilinear space-time phase saturates this bound for every admissible set of standard-deviation budgets, and that the bound therefore provides a necessary and sufficient condition for reaching a target information within the canonical model. For this state, the joint measurement of the arrival time and the transverse wave number is optimal among local Gaussian measurements, yields the Rényi-2 entropy of the reduced state, and attains the quantum Fisher information for the coupling at fixed input widths. We also show that, with additive detector noise, timing jitter limits the recorded information to a level set by the ratio of jitter to pulse duration. These results provide a framework for designing spatiotemporally coupled quantum signals, and we propose an optical realization based on pulse-front tilt and a lens.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Hypercubes and Beta--Gaussian Mixtures
papers.authors: Ali Darijani; Emadedin Soufian; Jürgen Beyerer
papers.abstract: We derive closed-form Gaussian information projections of Beta--Gaussian distributions whose tangential components are supported on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal components are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely characterized by moment matching, and the corresponding minimum Kullback--Leibler divergence admits an explicit expression depending only on the intrinsic Beta parameters, independently of the embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters. In the uniform case, this divergence reduces to a linear function of the intrinsic dimension. We further extend this construction to finite, pure embedded cubical complexes by considering mixtures of the componentwise Gaussian projections. Using the joint convexity of the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish an explicit upper bound on the approximation error of the resulting Gaussian Mixture. For uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the bound is linear in the intrinsic dimension and independent of the geometry of the complex, its embedding, and the normal Gaussian parameters.

papers.title: Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
papers.authors: Leonardo Vanni; Stefano Gasperini; Federico Tombari; Chiara Plizzari
papers.abstract: Reconstructing dynamic scenes and objects from monocular egocentric video is crucial for embodied AI, yet existing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approaches struggle with everyday interactions involving topological changes, such as cutting, assembly, opening, or closing. Since 4DGS methods rely on deforming a fixed representation, events that split, merge, or reveal surfaces cause severe visual artifacts. To address this challenge, we introduce TopoEgo, the first benchmark dedicated to topological changes in egocentric video (covering fission, fusion, open, and close), alongside Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware reconstruction method. Topo4DGS jointly models part-level motion and time-varying surface support by assigning independent rigid transformations to interacting parts and dynamically activating or deactivating Gaussians as surfaces appear, disappear, or separate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Topo-4DGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 4DGS approaches across topological changes, especially on post-event frames. Code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
papers.authors: Alejandro Cañada; Chema Garabito
papers.abstract: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons about and understands the image and its depth at the same time, and one set of weights generates images with their depth, estimates depth from photographs and paints images onto a given depth. At enough scale it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists on established depth benchmarks while keeping the generative abilities of the backbone it started from without specialized layers. We release two models for the community.

papers.title: Tests of Covariate Effects and Model Selection in Finite Mixture Regression Model
papers.authors: Chong Gan; Jacqueline May; Zeny Feng
papers.abstract: Finite mixture regression models are widely used to capture the heterogeneous effects of covariates on a response variable. Our study, motivated by the analysis of Chiroptera, explores the dynamic effects of various environmental, biological, and human-related covariates on the evolutionary development of bat forearm using finite Gaussian mixture regression (GMR) models. In this paper, we address two key questions: (1) which covariates are associated with the variation in forearm length; and (2) whether the associated covariates have the same effect across all subpopulations. To answer these questions, we propose two stepwise procedures within the finite GMR framework based on the weighted significance test (WEST): (1) a stepwise variable selection procedure to identify relevant influential covariates, and (2) a stepwise effect-type determination procedure to determine each relevant covariate as having either a homogeneous or heterogeneous effect across subpopulations. Based on these procedures, we introduce a stepwise model selection procedure for finite mixture regression, illustrated through finite GMR models. Simulation studies are conducted to assess the performances of our proposed procedures. The proposed procedure will be applied to the Chiroptera dataset.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.authors: Shantanu Deodhar
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$.   For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors
papers.authors: Fabien Casenave
papers.abstract: Engineering design studies produce a few tens to a few hundred simulations of one problem, each on its own mesh, and their surrogates are retrained for every study. Tabular foundation models instead infer a new task from its examples in one forward pass, after pretraining on synthetic tasks. We demonstrate the feasibility of in-context learning for physical field prediction on unstructured meshes. A single model, PhysICL, pretrained solely on procedural tasks, predicts fields, with quantiles, directly on each query mesh from labeled simulations, without updating its weights. The same checkpoint accepts variable numbers of context examples, scalar inputs and input fields, and any number of output fields, while mesh size and connectivity can vary within a task. Its procedural prior draws generic laws and boundary-element physical models on morphed 2D and 3D template meshes, evaluated only at the points the model samples, fast enough that tasks generated on the fly by CPU workers keep the GPUs busy throughout pretraining. On five PLAID datasets never seen in pretraining, its field error decreases as the context grows and, from $K = 32$, is below that of the nearest context simulation on every dataset and context draw. It is on par with per-dataset reduced-order models on two of them, behind them where the fields are low-rank. On AhmedML surfaces with a median of 1.1 million nodes, twenty times the largest pretraining mesh, its fixed spatial budgets keep the peak GPU memory at $K = 64$ at 4.27 GiB, against 4.07 GiB on the 6,000-node meshes of 2D\_MSHE. Finally, on 2D\_MSHE, far from the prior, fine-tuning on procedural tasks that reproduce its geometry and loads, without any of its outputs, at a tenth of the pretraining cost, divides the stress error by 2.7.

papers.title: Do magnetic cycles of Sun-like stars exhibit Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule?
papers.authors: Suyog Garg; Bidya Binay Karak
papers.abstract: One intriguing feature of the solar magnetic cycle is its alternating cycle amplitude: the even-numbered cycles are usually followed by stronger odd-numbered cycles, popularly known as the Gnevyshev-Ohl rule (or the even-odd effect). In this study, we probe whether Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends exist in stellar cycles of Sun-like stars, utilizing the Mount Wilson Observatory (MWO) chromospheric $S$-index data as a proxy for the stellar magnetic field. We apply quasi-Planck and skewed-Gaussian function fits to extract the cycle peaks from the MWO $S$-index data and consider the stars that have a minimum of four usable cycles. First, we say that Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule is obeyed in any star for a pair of even-odd or odd-even cycles, if the second cycle in the pair is stronger. For this definition, we find that many of the stars considered, especially slow rotators, hold the Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends quite well, with the fraction of cycles obeying the GO-rule been $1.0$ for these stars. However, we do not find any significant correlation between the fraction of cycles obeying the rule and the rotation period or the Rossby number of the star. Next, we examine Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule in the stellar cycles using alternative definitions for the rule. Saying that the rule holds as long as the middle cycle has a maximum or minimum in sets of consecutive three cycles, we obtain a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.25 $(p=0.299)$ and 0.59 (0.007), between the GO-rule fraction and the rotation period and Rossby number respectively, for the skewed-Gaussian fit data. Inspite of the fact, that our analysis suffers from a lack of sufficient number of good-quality cycles, we be believe that our results can still shed some light on the dynamo mechanism in other Sun-like stars and its dependence on rotation.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Modular Obstacle and Spatial-Aware Framework for Manipulation In Cluttered Scenes
papers.authors: Richard Shi; Mohammad Mahdavian; Mehrdad Momeni Zadeh; Mohammed Elmahgiubi; Amir Rasouli
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in robotic manipulation, yet most rely primarily on 2D visual observations and language instructions, leaving scene geometry and obstacle relationships to be inferred implicitly. This limitation is particularly problematic in cluttered environments, where small spatial errors can lead to unintended contacts or collisions. We propose MOSAIC, a modular spatial- and obstacle-aware framework that can be integrated with pretrained VLA policies to improve object-level scene understanding and action generation. Our method augments the VLA backbone with an auxiliary semantic grounding task that predicts role-specific masks for the target object, destination region, and surrounding obstacles. We further combine the target and destination masks with depth estimated from 3D scene reconstruction to construct role-specific geometric tokens that are injected directly into the action expert. In addition, we propose obstacle-aware attention supervision that emphasizes obstacles near the robot body during task execution. The resulting attention features are subsequently injected into later action-expert layers to further guide action generation. Together, these components provide explicit semantic, geometric, and obstacle-aware cues while preserving the underlying pretrained VLA architecture. We evaluate our framework on pretrained VLA model using the RoboPRO benchmark, including visual perturbation tests, and further validate it on real-world manipulation tasks. MOSAIC improves the success rate by 5.1% in cluttered scenes, and by 9.7% under visual perturbations, with gains of up to 25.0% in the most challenging environment. We will release our code and dataset upon acceptance at the following Github page: https://mmahdavian.github.io/MOSAIC/

papers.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
papers.authors: Alessandro Mariani
papers.abstract: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

papers.title: FastBox: A lightweight Python package for rapid cosmological 21cm intensity mapping simulations
papers.authors: Philip Bull; Bruno B. Bizarria; Melis O. Irfan; Geoff Murphy
papers.abstract: FastBox is a Python package for generating fast, physically realistic simulations of cosmological signals in three-dimensional co-moving boxes, with the primary focus of its application being 21cm intensity mapping (IM) experiments. It provides a framework for producing cosmology-dependent Gaussian and log-normal density fields, as well as modelling the effects of redshift-space distortions and linear biasing, among others. Models of instrumental systematics are incorporated, including radiometer noise and beam convolutions. Diffuse and point source foreground models are included, along with a number of foreground filtering strategies such as PCA, ICA, and transfer function correction via mock signal injection. Lastly, estimators are provided for power spectra, the two-point correlation function, and the equilateral bispectrum. The same underlying density field can also be Poisson-sampled into a discrete galaxy catalogue, so that 21cm and galaxy tracers are simulated from common initial conditions and their cross-power spectrum can be measured. Simulation grids may be cubic or anisotropic, with independent side lengths and cell counts along each Cartesian axis. FastBox is designed as a lightweight but realistic test-bench for the development and validation of end-to-end cosmological analysis pipelines.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
papers.authors: Akash Ashirbad Panda; Utpal Manna
papers.abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

papers.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward heavy-flavor correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
papers.authors: Farid Salazar; Björn Schenke; Wenbin Zhao
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-flavor azimuthal correlations as probes of gluon saturation in high-energy $p$+$p$ and $p$+Pb collisions within the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. Heavy flavor has several advantages: heavy-quark production is especially sensitive to the small-$x$ gluon distribution of the target, while the quark mass suppresses collinear radiation. Further, the heavy meson carries a large fraction of the momentum of its parent quark, so that the meson pair follows the partonic kinematics more closely than for light hadrons. We present the first calculation of heavy-meson pair correlations over the full azimuthal range that combines small-$x$ evolution from an initial condition constrained by HERA data with Sudakov resummation near the back-to-back limit. It provides a good description of the $D$-$\bar D$ and $b$-hadron pair correlations measured by LHCb. In contrast to the light-flavor case, we predict, in addition to a suppression of the away-side yield in $p$+Pb relative to $p$+$p$ collisions by about $15\%$, a broadening of the peak by approximately $10\%$ to $25\%$ for Gaussian fits near $ΔΦ=π$, which makes heavy-flavor correlations a promising observable in the search for gluon saturation.

papers.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
papers.authors: Shiyong Guo; Enrico Rinaldi; Jad C. Halimeh; Brian Swingle
papers.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
papers.authors: Euclid Collaboration; J. W. Nightingale; S. H. Vincken; L. R. Ecker; A. Nersesian et al.
papers.abstract: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.

papers.title: Automated identification of dipole mixed-modes in red-giant stars
papers.authors: Francisca Espinoza-Rojas; Michaël Bazot; Saskia Hekker; Sébastien Bourguignon
papers.abstract: Dipole mixed modes probe the internal structure of red giants by carrying information from both the convective envelope and the radiative core. Hence, identifying these modes allows for the determination of evolutionary states and stellar interior conditions. This identification typically relies on comparing observed frequencies with theoretical ones derived from the mixed-mode asymptotic relation. However, the process is challenging due to parameter-space degeneracies, stellar rotation, as well as missing modes and spurious peaks in the power density spectrum. In this work, we aim to develop an automated method for identifying dipole mixed modes, suitable for large-scale asteroseismic analyses. We introduce a metric that measures the overlap between observed and asymptotic dipole frequencies, represented as spike trains convolved with Gaussian kernels. After optimising this metric with a genetic algorithm, we use the best-fit parameters to perform a global assignment of the oscillation modes. We then validated the method using synthetic frequencies of RGB and CHeB stars perturbed by stellar rotation, and further tested it on four benchmark stars. Validation using perturbed synthetic frequencies shows that our method recovers over 95% of the dipole mixed modes across different evolutionary states, and this performance remains robust to spurious peaks and missing modes. For the benchmark stars, our dipole mode identification is consistent with previously published results, with mixed-mode parameter estimates typically agreeing within 1% for $ΔΠ$1 and 10% for $δν$rot and $q$. Our analysis demonstrates that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges associated with the complex dipole mode spectrum. Thus, it enables automated identification of dipole mixed modes, supporting homogeneous, large-scale asteroseismic analyses of evolved stars.

papers.title: Dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function in multiple-population globular clusters
papers.authors: J. Bruce; E. Vesperini; A. Askar; M. Giersz; E. Dalessandro et al.
papers.abstract: The dynamical evolution of globular clusters is significantly influenced by the multiscale structure introduced by the presence of multiple stellar populations. In this study, we investigate the long-term dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function (MF) within globular clusters hosting two stellar populations using a suite of Monte Carlo simulations run with the MOCCA code. Dynamical processes including two-body relaxation, mass segregation, and tidal stripping result in distinct radial profiles describing the variation with distance from the cluster's center of the stellar MF slope within the first population (P1), the second population (P2), and the cluster as a whole. We show that these radial profiles are well described by a broken power law with a knee located slightly interior to the half-mass radius, a feature partially driven by the multiscale structure of the multiple populations. In both 3D and 2D projected coordinates, we explore several characteristic clustercentric distances within the profile, including those where the local MF slope matches the global value of the present-day MF slope and the initial mass function (IMF) slope, and we examine how these positions evolve with the cluster's dynamical age. Our results highlight how the initially more centrally concentrated P2 drives a steeper radial gradient and a steeper MF slope in the outer regions, which subsequently affects the global cluster values. Motivated by recent observational studies suggesting that a bottom-light IMF may better describe massive globular clusters, as well as measurements of a flatter P2 MF slope in the outer regions of 47 Tucanae, we additionally explore a three-parameter bottom-light IMF and a simulation in which the P1 IMF differs from the P2 IMF, with the P2 IMF flatter than that of the P1 in the lower mass range.

papers.title: Sharp Lower Bounds for Parallel Log-Concave Sampling
papers.authors: Evan Dogariu
papers.abstract: How many rounds of parallel queries are needed to sample from a smooth, strongly log-concave distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$? For every fixed condition number $κ\in (1, \infty)$, we prove that any sampler making polynomially many queries per round requires $Ω_κ(\log d)$ rounds to achieve constant total variation error in the worst case. The lower bound holds even if queries return derivatives of all orders. Together with the first-order parallel Picard algorithm of \cite{zhou2025parallel}, this establishes a depth complexity of $Θ_κ(\log d)$ for parallel log-concave sampling with $\operatorname{poly}(d)$ width.   We then study centered Gaussian targets to understand how much width is needed at a given depth. From \cite{chewi2023query,zhou2026complexitygaussiansampling}, it is known that either one round of width $d$ or $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκ \log d)$ rounds of constant width suffice for first-order Gaussian sampling. At fixed $κ$ we characterize the depth-width tradeoff interpolating between these regimes: when using $ \lceil c \log d\rceil$ rounds, if $0 < c < c_\star(κ)$ then the optimal width at constant TV error is $\widetildeΘ(d^{1-c/c_\star(κ)})$, while if $c \geq c_\star(κ)$ then it is $Θ_κ(1)$. Here, $c_\star(κ)$ is an explicit constant with $c_\star(κ) \sim \sqrtκ / 8$ as $κ\to \infty$.

papers.title: Potts Order Preempts Emergence of 2-Form U(1) Spin Liquidity in Three-Dimensional Spin Vorticity Models
papers.authors: Michael D. Burke; Mohid U. Farooqi; Kristian Tyn Kai Chung; Michel J. P. Gingras
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin vorticity models (SVMs) have been proposed to realize an exotic 2-form U(1) classical spin liquid (CSL), characterized by a zero-curl constraint, string excitations, and deconfined fluctuating membranes. A previous numerical study [PRB 111, 064417 (2025)] uncovered a puzzle in the pyrochlore lattice SVM: despite exhibiting pinch points characteristic of a U(1) spin liquid, it also develops weak all-in--all-out (AIAO) order. Here, we show that the emergence of the 2-form CSL in 3D SVMs is preempted by an intrinsic instability towards entropy-driven height locking. We establish this by resolving the ground state constraints using a height mapping, which we further relate to a 3-state Potts antiferromagnet. This identifies the pyrochlore's weak AIAO order as permutationally symmetric sublattice (PSS) order, albeit with an exceptionally weak locking strength. We extend the SVM to lattices of corner-sharing octahedra and cubes, where we identify the alternative broken-sublattice-symmetry (BSS) order, a hidden order without magnetic Bragg peaks coexisting with collective paramagnetism. All three models undergo a 3D Ising transition consistent with a symmetry-allowed locking potential in the coarse-grained height theory. The spin liquid persists over intermediate length and temperature scales, but a critical Coulomb ground state ensemble fails to materialize, its correlations cut off by the finite locking length. These findings illustrate how microscopic constraints can determine the ultimate stability of emergent gauge theories in frustrated spin systems.

papers.title: A Latent Semiparametric Mixture Model for Robust Heterogeneity Learning in High Dimensions
papers.authors: Lyuou Zhang; Boxiang Wang; Lulu Wang; Wen Zhou; Hui Zou
papers.abstract: Learning heterogeneity from high-dimensional data has become a fundamental task across many data-driven fields. Cluster analysis is a widely used unsupervised tool for this purpose, and many existing methods have been adapted to high-dimensional settings through sparsity constraints. In contrast to algorithmic approaches, model-based clustering offers clean theoretical guaranties and computational simplicity, but can be restrictive in practice due to its reliance on specific parametric distributions. We propose a novel latent semiparametric mixture model for clustering, in which the observed data follow a Gaussian mixture after latent coordinate-wise monotone transformations. Furthermore, assuming a sparse optimal clustering rule in the latent space, we develop a new method, CESME, tailored for high-dimensional clustering. By allowing unspecified transformations, our framework becomes substantially more flexible and robust than traditional model-based approaches. The clustering error of CESME is shown to approach the optimal clustering error at a rate matching that obtained when the true transformations are known. Extensive simulations and real data analysis confirm that CESME outperforms a broad range of existing high-dimensional clustering methods, including those designed for single-cell RNA sequencing data. The online supplementary file contains technical proofs, additional discussions, and more numerical results.

papers.title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
papers.authors: Debsurya De; Dmitriy Kunisky
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{Ω(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $χ^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.

papers.title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
papers.authors: Peter Banda; John Caughman; Tobi Lehman
papers.abstract: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $σ$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,σ^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $σ^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.

papers.title: Large deviations of spatial moments of the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti lattice gas following a localized energy release
papers.authors: Timo Schorlepp; Baruch Meerson; Pavel Sasorov
papers.abstract: We study the long-time statistics of spatial moments of the time-dependent energy distribution in a one-dimensional Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti model following an instantaneous release of energy on a single lattice site. The moments are $M_n(T)=\sum_i x_i^n u_i(T)$, where $u_i(T)$ is the energy at site $i$ at the observation time $T$. Employing macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we calculate the variance of $M_n$ for every positive integer $n$ and determine the non-Gaussian distribution tails for the representative cases $n=1$ and $2$. For the first moment, we establish an exact duality, within MFT, to integrated-current statistics for a deterministic flat initial density. For both $n=1$ and $n=2$, the large-moment tails are dominated by a single adiabatically evolving doublon: a rapidly propagating pair of narrow solitary pulses of the energy density and of the gradient of the conjugate field. The small-second-moment tail is associated with concentration of the energy near the origin at time $T$. Comparing single- and two-doublon histories, we predict a dynamical phase transition at a critical value of $M_2$ at which the optimal path breaks reflection symmetry $x\to -x$. Numerical solutions obtained by direct minimization of the MFT action establish the second-order character of this transition and support our analytical predictions. Finally, we extend calculations of the large- and small-moment tails to arbitrary $n$ and numerically find a transition of the same type for $n=4$.

papers.title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
papers.authors: Feng Guo
papers.abstract: Bonnefont, Rajamäki and Vargas conjectured that, for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field, the Fourier dimension at $α+iβ$ equals the dimension of the real chaos at $α$ minus $β^2$. We prove the conjecture on the circle throughout their stated parameter range. For the canonical holomorphic family, the identity holds on one event of probability one for all $γ=α+iβ$ in the union of the open unit disk and the region $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$, $|α|+|β|<\sqrt2$. For each fixed parameter on the conjecture's sloping boundary, where $1<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|α|+|β|=\sqrt2$, the Fourier coefficients decay at a logarithmic rate almost surely and the Fourier dimension is zero. For nonzero interior parameters with $|α|\ne1/\sqrt2$, the critical Sobolev index is half the Fourier dimension minus $1/2$. The chaos fails to belong to the corresponding space when $|α|<1/\sqrt2$ and belongs to it when $|α|>1/\sqrt2$. For $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|β|\le\sqrt2-|α|$, we bound the Fourier coefficients at the decay power predicted by the dimension formula, up to logarithmic factors. For $0<|γ|<1$ and $α^2<1/2$, the measures obtained by multiplying the squared modulus of the smoothed chaos by $ε^{|γ|^2}$ converge weakly almost surely along $ε=e^{-m}$, uniformly on compact parameter sets, to explicit multiples of the real chaos at $2α$.

papers.title: Accelerating exact solutions of relativistic hydrodynamics and Levy-shaped freeze-out sources
papers.authors: Máté Csanád; Ágoston Benyó; Márton Nagy; Bence Szentkuti
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic measurements in heavy-ion collisions indicate that the pion source is Lévy-stable rather than Gaussian, while the source radii still follow the hydrodynamic scaling $R^2\propto 1/m_T$. We call this coexistence the Lévy hydro puzzle. For a perfect fluid with $\varepsilon=κp$ and $p=nT$, flow and pressure form a closed system, and density and temperature can be ``dressed'' by an arbitrary comoving function, generalising a freedom known from Hubble-type solutions to arbitrary flows. We show that, at nonzero pair momentum, the source is bounded by the pressure on the freeze-out hypersurface, so its tail can never be heavier than the pressure tail. This yields a criterion for power-law source tails with two routes: either the outer flow is ultra-relativistic and the temperature grows at least linearly (Hubble-type solutions), or the flow is slow, the temperature uniform, and the proper acceleration falls off as $1/r$. We present a new family of relativistic, accelerating, self-similar potential flows ($λ$-PF) and a new dressing of Gubser's flow. The acceleration of $λ$-PF generates no power-law tail, but with a Hubble-type dressing its source tail is Lévy-stable in a range of parameters, generalising the Hubble-type Lévy source to accelerating cores. The isothermally dressed Gubser flow realises the $1/r$ route: its tail exponent lies outside the Lévy-stable range, but over the measured range it gives Lévy-like sources with $1/R^2$ linear in $m_T$. Thus Lévy-like sources and the hydrodynamic $m_T$ scaling are compatible in perfect-fluid hydrodynamics, but hydrodynamics does not create the power-law tail: it is either inherited from a power-law pressure, requiring a $1/r$ acceleration, or put in through the dressing. We outline extensions towards non-spherical geometries and elliptic flow.

papers.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates
papers.authors: Alexander Gräfe; Max van Gemmeren; Paul Brunzema; Sebastian Trimpe
papers.abstract: Federated Bayesian Optimization (FedBO) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing Bayesian Optimization (BO) in distributed, privacy-sensitive settings, enabling agents to accelerate the optimization of their local objectives by sharing knowledge about their similarities without exposing raw data. However, existing methods rely on restrictive assumptions, such as near-identical objective functions or shared Gaussian process hyperparameters that are often violated in heterogeneous real-world applications. We present GLOBAFED, a novel framework that enables efficient knowledge transfer across different but related objectives without compromising privacy. At its core is a probabilistic neural network surrogate with a shared feature-extracting backbone and agent-specific heads equipped with varia- tional Bayesian last layers to provide uncertainty estimates. During optimization, agents use federated learning on the shared backbone to collaboratively build a common latent feature representation, while agent-specific heads adapt to their individual objectives. Our empirical results demonstrate that GLOBAFED significantly accelerates convergence and reaches better final performance compared to state-of-the-art FedBO baselines, and enables agents to warm-start their optimization from previously learned global features.

papers.title: CGOcc: Learning Cross-Gaussian Dependencies for 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction
papers.authors: Zirui Huang; Jiongle He; Yunfan Zeng; Yuanzhi Lu; Guangye Li et al.
papers.abstract: In Gaussian-based semantic occupancy prediction, overlapping primitives can provide ambiguous class predictions, making their joint interpretation important for voxel classification. However, current methods using spatially weighted mixtures neglect explicit modeling of cross-primitive dependencies, limiting the readout's ability to utilize category-specific relational evidence. Hence, we introduce CGOcc, a supervised multi-camera framework that explicitly models Cross-Gaussian dependencies for 3D semantic Occupancy prediction. CGOcc integrates appearance and geometric observations to refine Gaussian states and encodes cross-Gaussian dependencies in a diagonal-plus-low-rank representation. To incorporate these dependencies into voxel classification, CGOcc uses a class-conditional projection to extract diagonal and signed cross-Gaussian statistics without constructing a dense dependency matrix. The readout then refines occupied-class probabilities using these statistics while preserving a learned reference's occupied mass and free probability. Extensive experiments on nuScenes demonstrate CGOcc achieves state-of-the-art performance, with larger gains at high Gaussian overlap and improved predictions near boundaries. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of covariance-aware prediction and support its synergy with geometric interaction.

papers.title: Sliced Inverse Regression Revisited: When the Number of Predictors Grows Proportionally With the Sample Size
papers.authors: Peng Zeng; Hanwen Huang
papers.abstract: Li (1991) introduced sliced inverse regression (SIR) as a dimension reduction method and established its theoretical properties under the assumption that the number of predictors $p$ remains fixed as the sample size $n$ tends to infinity. In this paper, we revisit the theoretical properties of SIR in the high-dimensional regime where $p/n \to γ\in [0,1)$, assuming normally distributed predictors and a fixed number of slices. We show that the sample SIR eigenvalues exhibit an upward bias when $γ>0$, that their fluctuations are governed by the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble, and that the signal eigenvalues are asymptotically normal after an appropriate bias correction. We demonstrate that Li's chi-squared test requires a scaling adjustment to achieve the nominal asymptotic size when $γ>0$. We further propose two additional tests that achieve the nominal asymptotic size: an exact test based on Li's test statistic and a largest-eigenvalue test. In addition, we derive closed-form limits for the accuracy of the estimated SIR directions and show that their first-order expansions in $γ$ agree with Li's approximation. Finally, we establish the limiting distribution of the estimated sufficient predictors for a new observation and show that, when $γ>0$, they contain an additional independent Gaussian noise component. Simulation studies corroborate our theoretical findings.

papers.title: SpaceMCP: Vision Language Model Spatial Reasoning via Model Context Protocol
papers.authors: Ameen Izhac; Nobuko Yoshida; Ronald Clark
papers.abstract: Despite impressive advances in large language models (LLM), vision-language models (VLM) still exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities. Recent progress in feed-forward 3D reconstruction has enabled precise, real-time geometric understanding from visual inputs. In this work, we propose SpaceMCP, a framework that leverages these advances to introduce an MCP-style paradigm for spatial reasoning. Our approach augments a VLM with structured function calls, allowing it to query a scene graph for spatial information such as distances, object positioning, and camera properties. The scene graph is constructed in real time using feed-forward 3D reconstruction to recover metric geometry, combined with open-vocabulary segmentation to identify and localize relevant objects within the scene. Paired with the VLM's strong reasoning capabilities, the VLM is able to combine this primitive information to solve more complex spatial tasks. Without any training, SpaceMCP achieves state-of-the-art results on VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench and VSTI-Bench, outperforming recent spatially post-trained VLMs and improving its base VLM by 15-22 points per benchmark. We argue that, given the contrast between the relatively slow progress in native VLM spatial reasoning and the rapid advances in feed-forward 3D computer vision, this paradigm offers a promising path forward for enabling robust spatial reasoning.

papers.title: Empirical Bayes mirror testing for persistent widening of achievement gaps in U.S. school districts
papers.authors: Bowen Gang; Yin Xia
papers.abstract: Unequal recovery from pandemic learning losses raises concerns about widening achievement gaps between economically disadvantaged students and their peers. This study seeks to identify districts whose mathematics gaps widened in every annual interval from 2022 to 2025. The analysis uses estimates from the Stanford Education Data Archive (SEDA) for 5,600 U.S. school districts. Identifying such districts requires accounting for correlated errors and differing precision in the estimated annual changes, as well as multiplicity. The true annual gap changes in each district form an effect vector, and persistent widening means that every component is positive. To address this class of multiple testing problems, we propose an empirical Bayes mirror procedure. It uses an estimated distribution of effect vectors to guide ranking and covariance-adjusted mirror observations to calibrate selection. The procedure achieves finite-sample false discovery rate (FDR) control under a Gaussian observation model, without requiring accurate estimation of the posterior null probabilities used for ranking. Simulations demonstrate power gains from incorporating information about the distribution of effect vectors. At a target FDR of 25%, the SEDA analysis identifies eight districts in five states with evidence of widening gaps in every annual interval.

papers.title: Gradient-Free Inverse Design of 3D Nanophotonic Devices Using the Level-Set-Method
papers.authors: Oliver Kuster; Carsten Rockstuhl; Thomas Jebb Sturges
papers.abstract: Advances in 3D nanophotonic additive manufacturing enable increasingly complex, almost free-form devices for manipulating light at sub-wavelength scales. Extending nanophotonic designs into three dimensions introduces additional degrees of freedom. Exploiting this freedom requires inverse-design methods that can efficiently navigate this large design space while accommodating fabrication constraints. Here, we combine gradient-free optimization with the level-set method (LSM) to provide such an approach for 3D additive manufacturing. Representing the 3D geometry as a level set constructed from Gaussian radial basis functions retains substantial geometric freedom with only a few hundred design variables. This compact representation makes gradient-free optimization practical for fully 3D nanophotonic devices, eliminating the need for adjoint calculations. This unlocks the use of any Maxwell solver or auxiliary algorithms that should express fabrication constraints for which the required derivatives are unavailable or impractical to obtain, and enables embarrassingly parallel workflows. Consequently, binary fabrication requirements, such as structural connectivity, can be rigorously enforced, avoiding the differentiable approximations commonly used in gradient-based optimization. Here, we demonstrate the combination of the gradient-free LSM with a connected-component analysis algorithm to enforce the structural integrity of the design. We demonstrate the applicability of the gradient-free LSM by optimizing a Y-splitter while strictly enforcing the structural integrity of the material and the void in the design.

papers.title: Schwinger-Unruh Interplay and Mode-Resolved Entanglement of Charged Scalar Fields in Rindler Spacetime
papers.authors: Shagun Kaushal; Himanshu Parihar
papers.abstract: We study pairwise and cross-horizon correlations of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime in the presence of parallel electric and magnetic fields. The transverse magnetic field produces Landau levels, while the longitudinal mode problem follows the charged-scalar Rindler construction with the effective mass $M_n^2=m^2+(2n+1)|qB|$. For a specified global vacuum in the negative-frequency sector, we obtain the outgoing four-mode Gaussian state and calculate logarithmic negativity and quantum mutual information for selected mode pairs. We find that the cross-wedge antiparticle-particle pair is entangled only when $q_2<\tanh r_U$. It can therefore become separable although its mutual information remains nonzero. The intra-wedge particle-antiparticle pair remains entangled for nonzero Schwinger squeezing. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. We discuss the Landau-level dependence and the limits of these mode-resolved conclusions, without identifying the vacuum-dependent mixing parameter with a detector temperature.

papers.title: CoCode-World: Shared 3D Proxy Representation for Multi-Player World Models
papers.authors: Qirui Li; Xin Zhang; Yabo Chen; Jinkun Hao; Paul L Rosin et al.
papers.abstract: Multiplayer generative world models must produce observations that agree on shared entities despite different camera motions and occlusions. Explicit world representations provide spatial control, but precise modeling of individual game maps limits scene diversity, while shared geometry alone cannot ensure consistent appearance across views. We present CoCode-World, a shared 3D proxy framework that separates structural control from visual synthesis for two-player video generation. Programmable proxies specify scene layout, motion, and occlusion, while RGB references guide character and scene appearance. To coordinate visual details across players, we concatenate paired proxy videos, appearance references, and target views in a consistent spatial layout and generate both views jointly with a pretrained video model. This formulation uses the model's native attention for cross-view communication within a single generation branch, with LoRA adaptation learning proxy adherence and appearance correspondence from paired observations. We construct a two-player GTA~V dataset that pairs synchronized RGB observations with proxy videos derived from shared map geometry and game-engine state. Experiments demonstrate appearance transfer to characters and scene styles unseen during training, with improvements in video quality and cross-view player identity over the evaluated baseline. Ablations further examine how proxy construction and cross-view communication affect generation. Project page: https://iapple233.github.io/CCW/.

papers.title: Marginal-Preserving Coupled Diffusion Composition for Long-Horizon Planning
papers.authors: Hengrui Zhang; Qiyu Wang; Yuhu Cheng; Brooks Paige; Xuesong Wang
papers.abstract: Compositional diffusion planners extend short-horizon trajectory models to long-horizon goal-conditioned planning by generating and stitching multiple local trajectory chunks. However, in multimodal environments, local plausibility is not sufficient for global consistency: independently initialized chunks may denoise toward incompatible overlap modes, producing plans that are individually feasible but incoherent after stitching. Existing remedies typically add search, guidance, pruning, or graph-based structure at inference time, increasing computational cost or relying on task-specific machinery. We instead investigate graph-structured dependence among chunk-wise initial diffusion noises as a lightweight coordination mechanism for compositional trajectory planning. We propose \textbf{M}arginal-Preserving \textbf{C}oupled \textbf{D}iffusion \textbf{C}omposition (MCDC), a training-free inference method for pretrained compositional diffusion planners. Instead of sampling chunk noises independently, MCDC constructs coupled Gaussian initializations whose per-chunk marginals remain exactly standard Gaussian, as required by the pretrained denoiser, while neighboring chunks receive positively correlated noise components. This preserves the standard-Gaussian initialization marginal of each chunk while biasing adjacent chunks toward compatible overlap-mode choices. We prove exact marginal preservation and show, under a simple multimodal overlap model, that positive coupling increases the probability of compatible mode selection. On OGBench long-horizon stitch tasks, MCDC consistently improves over independent compositional diffusion sampling while retaining nearly the same inference time, and achieves a favorable success--cost trade-off compared with search-based composition methods.

papers.title: Measuring Milky Way Mass with RR Lyraes and Blue Horizontal Branch Stars
papers.authors: Xiangyu Li; Yang Huang; Jifeng Liu; Xinyi Li; Qikang Feng et al.
papers.abstract: Measuring the mass of the Milky Way is essential for understanding galaxy formation and evolution, characterizing the Galactic potential and assembly history, and probing the nature of dark matter. We derive the enclosed mass profile of the Milky Way out to Galactocentric distances of $\sim80\,\mathrm{kpc}$ using two halo tracers with full 3D kinematics: RR Lyraes (RRLs) and blue horizontal-branch stars (BHBs). Our sample consists of 7,550 RRLs and 8,230 BHBs constructed from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), spanning Galactocentric distances from $10$ to $100\,\mathrm{kpc}$. We estimate the enclosed mass using two independent methods: the spherical Jeans equation and the tracer mass estimator (TME). The two tracers yield consistent results, with $M(<81.7\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.76 \pm 0.23)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M(<82.8\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.66 \pm 0.35)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. Adopting an NFW profile to extrapolate the enclosed mass beyond the outermost radius probed by our tracers, we infer virial masses of $M_{200} = 8.12^{+0.72}_{-0.65}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 8.13^{+0.78}_{-0.67}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. We further validate our methodology using mock RRL and BHB samples constructed from two Auriga halos, finding that the inferred masses are underestimated by $15.5\%\pm2.8\%$ for RRLs and $11.9\%\pm3.4\%$ for BHBs, respectively. After correcting for these systematic errors, the Milky Way virial masses are $M_{200} = 9.79^{+0.93}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 9.24^{+0.95}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs.

papers.title: Quantum non-Gaussian coherence via dissipation to single qubits
papers.authors: Sirachat Kaewkongtham; Kimin Park; Darren W. Moore; Atirach Ritboon; Radim Filip
papers.abstract: Quantum non-Gaussian (QNG) coherence is a critical resource for advanced quantum technologies with bosonic systems, operationally distinct from the coherence provided by Gaussian states. For many experimental platforms, its deterministic generation remains a formidable experimental challenge. Here we propose that pulsed Gaussian control of a linear oscillator alternating with dissipation by the smallest nonlinear element -- an unmeasured ground-state qubit coupled via resonant Jaynes-Cummings (JC) interactions -- deterministically generates high-order QNG coherence. Although such dissipative processes are phase-insensitive and do not generate local coherence alone, when added to Gaussian operations they deterministically produce high-quality binary superpositions of lower Fock states $(|0\rangle + |N\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ up to $N=4$ with high fidelity ($\mathcal{F} > 0.98$), certified by the QNG coherence hierarchy, as well as binomial code states and logical magic states with high fidelity ($\mathcal{F} > 0.98$).

papers.title: SCR-Mamba: Skeleton-conditioned Mamba with cross-scale incremental refinement for efficient 3D human pose estimation
papers.authors: Jie Wang; Xuejing Gu; Congzhe Zhang; Zibo Zhao
papers.abstract: Mamba-based methods for video-based 3D human pose estimation can model long sequences with linear complexity, but their selective state updates usually lack direct exploitation of skeletal relations. Meanwhile, stacking modeling blocks at the full temporal resolution leads to high computational overhead, while compressing the temporal sequence makes it difficult to retain per-frame details. To address these issues, we propose SCR-Mamba, whose core consists of Skeleton-Conditioned State Modeling (SCSM) and Cross-Scale Incremental Refinement (CSIR). SCSM generates a skeleton context from bone connections and left-right symmetry relations and generates the selective parameters of the spatial and temporal branches conditioned on it, so that structural relations are involved in the writing, propagation, and reading of state information. CSIR constructs multi-scale motion representations through content-adaptive aggregation and progressively refines the retained per-frame features with the increments produced by coarse-scale modeling, integrating long-range motion context while reducing full-resolution computation. On Human3.6M with Stacked Hourglass (SH) 2D detections and 243-frame inputs, SCR-Mamba-L achieves 36.8 mm MPJPE (P1) with 7.72 M parameters and 15.10 G MACs, less than 1/7 of the computational cost of StructMamPose-L with similar accuracy; SCR-Mamba-X further reaches 36.6 mm P1 and 30.9 mm P-MPJPE (P2), achieving state-of-the-art performance. On MPI-INF-3DHP, SCR-Mamba-X achieves a percentage of correct keypoints (PCK) of 99.3%, an area under the curve (AUC) of 88.1%, and an MPJPE of 14.2 mm.

papers.title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
papers.authors: Connor Gäde; Matthias Kerzel; Hauke Bünning; Jan-Gerrit Habekost; Mariana Barros et al.
papers.abstract: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state. When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.

papers.title: Probe Dynamics in Active Baths via Trajectory-Response Relations
papers.authors: Chul-Ung Woo; Jiwon Choi; Heiko Rieger
papers.abstract: Passive probes in active baths can undergo spontaneous motion driven by nonequilibrium forces that depend on probe velocity and interaction geometry. Using trajectory-response relations that express the bath response to a probe in terms of free-particle displacement statistics, we investigate the dynamics of freely moving probes weakly coupled to ideal active baths. The mean force exerted by the bath defines a velocity-space potential whose minima describe the stable states. By analyzing how the mean force depends on the probe velocity, we identify stable resting and moving states and determine the parameter regime in which they coexist. For elliptical interactions, the resting state becomes unstable first along the narrow axis, resulting in direction selection already at the linear-response level. For fourfold interactions, linear friction remains isotropic, while the nonlinear dependence of the mean force on probe velocity selects axial or diagonal motion and produces directional multistability. We further show that the trajectory-response relations extend to higher orders in the probe strength, where multi-interval free-particle trajectory statistics become relevant. For a Gaussian probe, these higher-order terms shift the speed of the stable moving state.

papers.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
papers.authors: Stefan A. Kurlyand; Arkady A. Tseytlin
papers.abstract: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.

papers.title: Escaping the Curse of Dimensionality in One-Step Flow-Based Generative Models
papers.authors: Konstantin Yakovlev
papers.abstract: Flow and diffusion-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art quality, but require multiple forward passes at inference time, making them computationally costly. Consistency models overcome this by learning a flow map directly, enabling few-step generation and dramatically reducing the computation needed at test time. However, formal statistical guarantees for such one-step generators are scarce. Existing results either suffer from the curse of dimensionality or rely on impractical loss functions. We investigate whether one-step flow-based models can escape the curse of dimensionality under the assumption that the data distribution is generated by a low-dimensional surface perturbed with Gaussian noise. In this setup, we derive approximation and generalization error bounds for the flow map estimate that circumvent the curse of dimensionality. Our findings provide the first principled explanation for practical success of one-step flow-based generative models.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian approximation for Polyak--Ruppert averaged linear stochastic approximation
papers.authors: Bogdan Butyrin; Eric Moulines; Alexey Naumov; Sergey Samsonov
papers.abstract: We study how quickly the normalized Polyak--Ruppert average approaches its Gaussian limit in linear stochastic approximation with bounded i.i.d.\ coefficients. For step sizes decaying as $k^{-γ}$, with $1/2\leγ<1$, we prove an upper bound of order $n^{γ-1}$ on the approximation error over convex sets in fixed dimension. A matching lower bound holds for every fixed model. The fastest rate in this range is $n^{-1/2}$, attained at $γ=1/2$. We also obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound on the error of the recursive multiplier bootstrap procedure.

papers.title: ThermalSplat: Generalizable Pose-Free Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Thermal 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Prasanna S; Gopi Raju Matta; Divya Madhuri Vemunuri; Kaushik Mitra
papers.abstract: Thermal infrared imaging is vital for applications like search-and-rescue and autonomous navigation, yet trans- lating it into 3D scene representations remains a critical bottleneck. The low-texture nature and view-dependent emissivity of thermal images cause standard pose estima- tors to fail catastrophically, collapsing standard 3D Gaus- sian Splatting pipelines under sparse-view constraints. Fur- thermore, existing thermal reconstruction methods rely heavily on dense capture and computationally expensive per-scene optimization. Critically, many of these ap- proaches depend on aligned RGB-thermal datasets to ob- tain reliable camera poses and initial point clouds, ren- dering them unusable in purely thermal, unposed envi- ronments. To break this bottleneck, we present Thermal- Splat, the first generalizable, feed-forward Gaussian splat- ting framework that reconstructs 3D scenes directly from sparse thermal images without requiring known camera poses, RGB guidance, or per-scene training. We over- come thermal-specific challenges using a soft census loss for brightness-invariant structural matching and a bound- ary structure loss to explicitly supervise temperature discon- tinuities. Trained on an aggregated multi-source dataset, ThermalSplat synthesizes sharp reconstructions of unseen scenes in a single feed-forward pass. Extensive experi- ments demonstrate that ThermalSplat holds a strict advan- tage over scene-specific thermal splatting methods in the sparse regime. Furthermore, even compared against these baselines operating under their ideal dense capture set- tings, ThermalSplat achieves superior perceptual fidelity. By eliminating the need for computationally expensive per scene optimization, ThermalSplat offers an efficient and generalizable approach to thermal 3D reconstruction.

papers.title: IncR-3DSGG: Incremental Posed RGB Image Based 3D Scene Graph Generation via Privileged Depth Supervision
papers.authors: Mrunmai Phatak; Daniel Kienzle; Roman Küble; Jörg Hähner; Rainer Lienhart
papers.abstract: Scene graphs provide a compact, structured representation of environments by capturing objects and their spatial or semantic relationships in a form suitable for embodied agents. Existing 3D scene graph generation methods often rely on depth sensing at inference, either to associate object instances across views via point cloud overlap or to compute inter-object relations from geometric cues, limiting deployment to platforms with depth sensors. We propose IncR-3DSGG, which builds 3D scene graphs incrementally from posed\footnote{RGB images with camera extrinsics estimated by an off-the-shelf visual SLAM system.} RGB images, eliminating the use of depth sensors at inference. Our method leverages a Parametric Relation Predictor (PRP) that learns to estimate pairwise distances and relative angles between objects from 2D visual features and 2D geometric cues, using 3D geometric supervision available only during training. These learned pairwise measurements are fused across views through Pose Graph Optimization (PGO)~\cite{grisetti2010tutorial} to recover metrically grounded 3D object positions and build a globally consistent 3D scene graph incrementally. On the real-world 3RScan~\cite{wald2019rio} dataset, our method attains $52.2$ mean object recall and $30.8$ mean predicate recall under the 3DSSG~\cite{wald2020learning} evaluation protocol, against $27.0$ and $17.6$ for MonoSSG~\cite{wu2023incremental}, while using no depth or reconstructed geometry at inference. This shows that relations and metrically grounded 3D object representations can be predicted from posed RGB images alone.

papers.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
papers.authors: Zixuan Qiu; Pengshuai Shi; Ruijun Wu
papers.abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

papers.title: $r$-Largest Order Statistics for Galaxy Cluster Cosmology I: Reconstruction of the high-mass end of the Halo Mass Function
papers.authors: T. Gayoux; P-S. Corasaniti
papers.abstract: We introduce the $r$-largest order statistics ($r$-LOS) framework for galaxy clusters, a generalization of the standard extreme value statistics (EVS) approach. While conventional EVS focuses on the probability distribution of the most massive cluster within a given volume, the $r$-LOS framework exploits the additional statistical information encoded in the joint distribution of the $r$ most massive clusters, ranked in descending order of mass. We develop the corresponding mathematical formalism, discuss its asymptotic properties, and derive a set of relations relevant to galaxy cluster cosmology. In particular, we demonstrate that the high-mass end of the halo mass function (HMF) can be reconstructed from the generalized extreme value (GEV) parameters inferred using an extension of the block maxima method that incorporates the $r$ most massive clusters in each volume. This provides a means of recovering the high-mass tail of the HMF using only a small subsample of the halo population. We validate these relations using both comoving and light-cone halo catalogues from numerical simulations. Finally, we investigate the sensitivity of the $r$-LOS framework to primordial non-Gaussianity, focusing on its impact on the statistics of massive clusters.

papers.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $χ$EFT and lattice QCD
papers.authors: Md. Emanuel Hoque; Arunava Mukherjee; Sayantan Sharma
papers.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

papers.title: Anisotropy driven critical phenomena in a van der Waals ferromagnet
papers.authors: Neesha Yadav; Harish Chandr Chauhan; Pintu Das
papers.abstract: We report a detailed investigation into the field-dependent critical behavior of the van der Waals ferromagnet $\mathrm{Fe_3GeTe_2}$ to elucidate how applied magnetic fields ($B$), strong magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and emerging other energy scales modulate its critical behavior. Utilizing the recently developed method, viz., the average of normalized slope (ANS), for analysis of critical behavior, we evaluate the critical exponents ($β$, $γ$, and $δ$) across distinct field windows up to $\rm{7\,T}$.
